title.narrative: Support to strengthen UN peace operations 2025-2026

description.narrative:
This Agreement covers extrabudgetary support to the UN Department of Peace Operations (UNDPO) with the aim to strengthen the capacity of UN peace operations to support the promotion of peace and security in host countries, thereby facilitating economic and social development in those countries. Three projects will be supported over the two-year period:
1. Strategic Rapid Response in Fragile Post-Conflict Settings (2026-2027) Implemented by DPO’s Justice and Corrections Standing Capacity (JCSC), the Standing Capacity for Security Sector Reform and Governance (SSuRGe Team), and the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration Standing Capacity (DDRSC), this project aims to deploy specialized civilian expertise to fragile post-conflict and transitional contexts. Its overarching impact is to strengthen the civilian capacity of UN peace operations to consolidate peace and prevent relapse into conflict, thus supporting sustainable development in host countries.
2. Advancing Implementation of the Conflict-Related Sexual Violence Mandate in Peacekeeping (2026–2027) This project aims to strengthen UN peacekeeping operations’ ability to prevent and respond to conflict-related sexual violence through capacity development, guidance, and advocacy. Managed by DPO’s Policy, Evaluation and Training Division (DPET) and its Policy, Best Practices, and Partnerships Section (PBPS), it translates the CRSV mandate into operational results across missions.
3. Implementing and Mainstreaming the Child Protection Mandate in Peacekeeping Operations (2026) Complementing the CRSV project, the child protection (CP) initiative reinforces the UN’s commitment to the protection of children affected by armed conflict and the operationalization of the CP mandate across missions. Implemented by DPO’s DPET/PBPS teams, it focuses on enhancing peacekeeping personnel’s knowledge and practical ability to integrate child protection into their daily work.
